1.explanation: All of the accessibility and rendering logic for the React ExpandableTile lives in Tile.js – this is where the role=button wrapper, aria-expanded attribute, and focusable elements are defined. Tile-test.js contains the unit tests for this component, which will need to be updated to cover the new screenreader behaviors (announcing the above-the-fold content on entry, reporting aria-expanded state, and preventing below-the-fold content from being exposed before expansion). Tile-story.js demonstrates the component in Storybook, so it should be updated to showcase and validate the corrected accessibility behavior as part of the manual review process.
1.bug_scenario: When you load the page and invoke VoiceOver (VO) and tab into the ExpandableTile, VO lands on the “Above the fold content” text as a generic text element (reporting “You are currently on a text element.”) instead of announcing it as part of an ExpandableTile. VO never reads out “Above the fold content” on entry, and when you navigate with VO’s Right‐Arrow, it reads: “Expand button main,” then “Above the fold content,” and immediately “Below the fold content” even though the tile is still collapsed. The button’s aria-expanded state is never spoken when the button first receives focus, and the below‐the‐fold content becomes exposed to VO before the user actually expands the tile.

2.explanation: All of the accessible behavior for ExpandableTile lives in Tile.js (the onClick/onKeyPress handlers, aria-expanded on the container and chevron button, aria-labelledby, and the logic for showing above- and below-the-fold content). index.js simply re-exports the component, so any changes to import paths or types live there. Tile-test.js contains the unit tests for ExpandableTile’s keyboard interactions and ARIA attributes, which will need updating to assert the new announcement order and aria-expanded behavior.
2.bug_scenario: When navigating to an ExpandableTile with VoiceOver or JAWS, the screen reader does not announce the “Above the fold” text on entry, it only reads the container role=“button” label. It also fails to include aria-expanded=false on the button announcement, and doesn’t require the user to toggle the tile before reading the “Below the fold” content. In practice VO/JAWS focus moves from the tile container straight to the “Below the fold content” when it isn’t expanded, and never reads the initial content until after expansion.
